newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian students see red over opposition's banner.
newsitem.headline: Serbian students see red over opposition's banner.

text.p: Serbian student protesters who thrive on close-quarter standoffs with police objected on Monday to opposition leaders' unfurling of a long, red banner between demonstrators and policemen.

Vuk Draskovic, a leader of the opposition coalition campaigning to restore its victories in annulled November municipal elections, proposed using the banner to replace the police, who had blocked the students from marching all night.

The students, who also have been demonstrating for more than two months, customarily end their protest in the early morning after the police cordon is removed. But police did not withdraw on Monday morning, so the standoff continued.
Draskovic said that by unfurling the banner to represent the police cordon, the policemen "can go and drink a beer if they like -- the street will be blocked by our cordon".
The banner was unfurled, but leaders of the student protest objected because they said it suggested strong links between the students and Zajedno.
The students support Zajedno's goal of reinstating the election results in which opposition victories in 14 cities were annulled but say their protest is not political.
In the end the banner, which police also feared could spark incidents, was taken away.
Police also arrested a student protester, Zoran Trifkovic, 25, who had stripped to his underwear because the police were blocking the student march, witnesses said.
The witnesses said police arrested and roughed up Trifkovic after he left the main demonstration and was walking through a tunnel under Terazije square.
Police had no immediate statement on the arrest.
